title: Registering, test day and Home Edition checklist
lines: Good preparation can be wasted by a problem on test day: the wrong ID, a computer that fails the check, or arriving late. This checklist covers what to do before you register, the week before, and on the day, for both test centers and Home Edition. Rules change, so treat this as a reminder list and confirm every detail on ets.org.
## Before you register
- Check what each target institution needs: the overall band, any section minimums, whether it accepts Home Edition, whether it accepts MyBest scores, and its application deadline.
- Work backward from the earliest deadline. Scores reach your ETS account about 3 days after the test, and institutions may take longer to process them. Leave time for a second attempt if possible.
- Decide between a test center and Home Edition. A test center gives you a controlled room and equipment. Home Edition saves travel but needs a suitable room, computer and internet connection.
- Check the current fee, payment options and rescheduling rules on ets.org. They differ by country and change over time.
- Check the ID rules for your country on ets.org. The name on your registration must match your ID exactly, so check spelling, the order of names and any middle name.
! Make sure the name in your ETS account matches your passport or other accepted ID letter for letter. A mismatch is one of the most common reasons test takers are turned away.
## Score reports

You can send 4 free score reports, and you must choose the institutions by 10 pm on test day. Prepare the list of institutions (and their codes, if required) before the test so you do not have to decide in a hurry. Extra reports cost US$25 each.
## The week before
- Take your last full mock no later than 2 or 3 days before the test, so you are not tired on the day.
- Review your notes on templates for Write an Email and Academic Discussion, and your Interview answer pattern.
- Plan the route to the test center and the travel time, or set up and test your Home Edition room.
- Sleep at your normal time. Do not try to learn large lists of new words in the last two days.
## Home Edition checklist

Home Edition is the same test taken on your own computer with a live remote proctor watching through your webcam. Check the exact equipment and room requirements on ets.org, and run any system check ETS provides well before test day and again the day before. In general you should expect to need:
- A computer that meets ETS requirements (check which operating systems and browsers are supported).
- A working webcam, microphone and speaker or headphones as allowed by the rules.
- A stable internet connection. If possible, use a wired connection and ask others at home not to stream video during your test.
- A quiet, private room with a clear desk and a closed door. Nobody else may enter during the test.
- An accepted ID document.
- Approved note-taking materials. Check on ets.org what is allowed at home, because it may be different from a test center.

! Power cuts and slow internet are real risks in many places. Charge your laptop fully, keep it plugged in, and if load shedding is common in your area, check the schedule and book a time when power is most reliable or consider a test center.
## Test center checklist
- Confirm the address, arrival time and what you may bring.
- Bring your accepted ID. Keep it with you until check-in.
- Arrive early. Late arrival can mean you are not allowed to test.
- Expect your personal items, including your phone, to be stored away during the test.
- Note-taking materials are normally provided at the center; do not bring your own paper unless the rules say you may.
## On the day
- Eat a normal meal and drink some water. There is no scheduled break, and the whole session takes about 2 hours including check-in and directions.
- Use the bathroom before you start.
- Wear comfortable clothes in layers; rooms can be cold or warm.
- During the test, follow the on-screen timer, not your own estimate.
- If something goes wrong (a sound problem, a frozen screen), tell the proctor or administrator at once rather than trying to fix it yourself.
## After the test
- Choose your free score report recipients by 10 pm on test day if you have not already.
- Check your ETS account for scores about 3 days later.
- If your score is below target, review it by section and plan your next attempt with the "Using your mock results" method.
